the growth of C6 cells is stimulated by VIP and PACAP but not by PHI, whereas the VIP antagonist neurotensin- VIP and both GRF analogues are able to inhibit VIP- and PACAP-induced cell growth stimulation.

the VIP-PACAP family of neuropeptides stimulates the growth of the C6 glioblastoma cells in vitro and that these effects are correlated with the expression by C6 cells of high-affinity polyvalent VIP-PACAP receptors and of VIP-selective very high-affinity binding species.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel subtype of VIP-PACAP receptor on C6 glioblastoma cells, which is involved in the regulation of cell growth and proliferation.
the identification of VIP receptors in C6 glioblastoma cells and with their correlation with the effects of the VIP family peptides on cell growth.
the effects of neuropeptides on cell growth, which are mediated by specific receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VIP-PACAP receptors mediate a stimulatory action on the growth of C6 glioblastoma cells in vitro, which is antagonized by neurotensin and GRF derivatives.

VIP and PACAC are able to stimulate the growth of C6 cells by acting on two subtypes of VIP receptors, one of which is a polyvalent highaffinity VIP-PAC1 receptor and the other one a very high-affinity selective VIP receptor.

VIP and PAC-AP are able to stimulate C6 cell proliferation by means of the activation of polyvalent and very high-affinity receptors, whereas the antagonist effects of both GRF peptides and of neurotensn-VIP are mediated by a very high-affinity, VIP-selective receptor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the VIP-PACAP system is involved in the control of the proliferation of glioblastoma cells in vitro, possibly through the activation of a VIP-selective binding site.
VIP and PACAC are mitogenic for C6 glioma cells, and the effects of the VIP-related peptides on C6 cell growth are correlated to the expression of high-affinity VIP/PACAP receptors.
VIP and PACAC are able to stimulate C6 cell proliferation through the activation of polyvalent VIP-PACAP receptors and that VIP antagonists can inhibit this effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VIP and related peptides can exert growth-promoting effects on glioblastomas in vitro, and that this effect is mediated by VIP-PACAP receptors.
the VIP/PACAP family of peptides can be used to modulate cell growth in C6 glioblastoma cells.
VIP and PACAC are potent stimulants of C6 cell growth in vitro, and that their effects are mediated, at least in part, by high-affinity VIP binding sites.
